note: The evergreen audit's Tier 2, its 'More cultivars' row and the deciduous conifers (Nov 2026). Sizes and zones are the Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder unless an estimate says otherwise, cross-checked against NC State Extension, the RHS and nursery listings. heightIn and spread are a planning size: a typical garden-lifetime tree, not the record tree, so a range is not always quoted at its midpoint; each estimate says why. px-art h/cw were solved with dev/cultivar-size.cjs, never set by eye: a species against the nearest existing tree of its habit, a cultivar against its own species.

estimates.size: MBG 15-30 x 6-12 ft, slowly to 50 ft. 25 x 10 ft.
estimates.cones: MBG: purple cones while still young, upright as on every fir.
estimates.culture: MBG: cool, moist, acid soil; not for the hot, humid summers south of zone 7.

estimates.size: MBG 20-30 x 10-18 ft, about 8 ft in ten years. 20 x 10 ft, under the species' planning size.
estimates.name: MBG lists it as 'Silberlocke', formerly 'Horstmann's Silberlocke', introduced by Gunter Horstmann in 1986.

estimates.culture: MBG: cool climates; not for hot, humid summers south of zone 5.

estimates.size: MBG 35-50 x 15-25 ft, about 50 x 20 ft in cultivation. 45 x 20 ft.
estimates.range: Caucasus and Turkey. The Caucasus is Asia-Temperate in the botanical regions (WGSRPD), so it is recorded as Asian, not European.

estimates.size: MBG 40-90 x 20-40 ft; 40-50 ft in cultivation, 90 ft or more wild. It is mostly an existing tree on a lot, so 60 x 30 ft.
estimates.culture: MBG: medium to wet soil, hot humid summers, mild winters; commonly self-seeds into old fields.

estimates.roles: MBG tolerates deer and drought; 'dry' and 'deerOk' follow it.
estimates.name: Wikipedia: called Norway pine in Minnesota.

estimates.size: Not in MBG. Water-wise guides 10-25 x 10-30 ft; other listings to 35-45 ft. A slow tree, so 20 x 18 ft.
estimates.culture: USU: trees in developments often do poorly from over-watering; Colorado guidance: not in regularly irrigated landscapes.

estimates.size: MBG 30-50 x 20-35 ft, slow. 35 x 25 ft.
estimates.bark: MBG: exfoliating patchwork of white, olive, light purple and silver, milky white at maturity, after ten years or more. Drawn with the new 'patchwork' bark style.
estimates.habit: MBG: most often multi-trunked; needles in threes.

estimates.size: MBG 30-50 x 30-50 ft in cultivation, 90 ft wild. Slow, and kept smaller in Japanese gardens, so 30 x 30 ft.
estimates.culture: MBG: cool summers; dislikes the heat and humidity of the deep South.

estimates.size: NC State 50-70 x 15-25 ft; MBG 50-70 ft in cultivation. 55 x 20 ft.
estimates.culture: NC State: likely not to thrive in the hot, humid Southeast; shelter from winter wind. MBG: tolerates poor, rocky soil.

estimates.size: MBG 10-35 x 4-12 ft, 8-10 ft in ten years. 25 x 10 ft.
estimates.colour: MBG: exterior needles bright yellow in sun, fading as summer goes on; can burn in hot sun; red pollen cones in spring.

estimates.group: Black Hills spruce, Dwarf Alberta and Big Berta, already in the catalog, are selections of it.

estimates.size: MBG 40-60 x 30-40 ft, the size the Glauca Group record already carries. 50 x 35 ft.
estimates.colour: MBG: seed-raised trees vary from green to silver-blue; this is the green one.
estimates.culture: MBG: tolerant of hot, humid summers, not reliably hardy at the cold end of its range.

estimates.size: MBG 30-50 ft (less often 90), text 'columnar with a steeple-like crown'; FNPS 20-40 (60) x 10-20 ft. MBG and NC State list a 30-40 ft spread, which does not fit the columnar habit they describe, so 40 x 15 ft follows FNPS.
estimates.deer: NC State: deer often damage it in winter.

estimates.size: MBG 40-60 ft in cultivation, narrow-pyramidal with short spreading branches. Its listed spread (30-60 ft) and NC State's (30-57 ft) are for wild trees of 110-175 ft; no published garden spread was found, so 15 ft is an estimate from the narrow habit.
estimates.disease: NC State: Phytophthora lateralis is a big problem; resistant rootstocks exist.

estimates.size: NC State 40-70 x 20-80 ft; UF 40-70 x 30-40 ft. 50 x 30 ft.
estimates.invasive: Cal-IPC: rated Limited; spreads from planted windbreaks into coastal prairie elsewhere in California. Not a serious invader, so it is in, with the warning in its blurb.
estimates.culture: NC State: canker more likely away from cool coastal breezes; has not done well in hot-summer areas.

estimates.size: RHS: higher than 12 m and 4-8 m across after more than 50 years; UK retailers: rarely past 8 m x 2.5 m. 25 x 8 ft in a garden lifetime, the audit's 15-25 ft.
MBG 40-90 x 15-25 ft, slow. 50 x 20 ft.
estimates.name: MBG files it as Xanthocyparis nootkatensis; the catalog keeps Callitropsis, as its weeping selection does, with the others as synonyms.
estimates.culture: MBG: some afternoon shade in the south of its range.

estimates.size: MBG 60-275 x 25-60 ft; in the eastern US typically only 40-60 ft. 80 x 30 ft for a garden lifetime where it grows well.
estimates.culture: MBG: best in cool, moist climates; intolerant of temperature extremes; not recommended for St. Louis.
estimates.drawing: Young trees are branched to the ground, so the scale habit is honest at planning size; the tall clear trunk of an old tree is left for the renderer.

estimates.size: MBG 60-100 x 15-25 ft; 60-90 ft in cultivation. 80 x 25 ft.
estimates.culture: MBG: cool, moist coastal climates; hardy to the deep South but does not grow well there.
estimates.resprouting: Wikipedia: resprouts from the base and burls after cutting or fire.

estimates.size: MBG 40-80 x 15-30 ft, typically 40-60. 50 x 20 ft.
estimates.season: MBG: needles turn a showy yellow in fall before dropping.
estimates.culture: MBG: boggy and wet soils; performs poorly south of zone 5.

estimates.invasive: Wikipedia: naturalized in Maine, Michigan, New York and New England; no US list calls it invasive (it is a wilding conifer in New Zealand). In, with the naturalization in its blurb.

estimates.season: MBG: light green in spring, deep green in summer, red-bronze in fall; trunk fluted at the base with age.

estimates.change: Already in the catalog; now opts into the leaf cycle (look.deciduous). Sizes unchanged.

estimates.size: Not in MBG. Calscape 25-82 x 15-40 ft; UC Berkeley 20-40 ft, sometimes 80; Boething 70 x 80 ft. Often as wide as tall in the open: 40 x 40 ft.
estimates.zones: Oregon State: hardy to zone 8; Devil Mountain 8-10; others 9-11. 8-10.
estimates.range: California Floristic Province, into Baja California, so North America and Mexico.
estimates.culture: UC IPM and UC Oaks: frequent summer irrigation near the trunk promotes Armillaria and Phytophthora root and crown rot.
MBG: acid, dry to medium, well-drained soil; drought tolerant; avoid wet soil; planted from Maryland to California.
estimates.bloom: Catkins in April, inconspicuous: no calendar slot, as for the other oaks.

estimates.size: MBG 15-20 x 10-15 ft, to 40 ft as a tree; NC State 15-35 x 15-20 ft. 25 x 18 ft.
estimates.bloom: NC State March-April; MBG February-April. March-April.
estimates.weedy: NC State: can become weedy from suckering and self-seeding.
estimates.toxicity: NC State: high severity; cyanogenic glycosides in stems, leaves and seeds, especially wilting material; a problem for cats, dogs and horses.

estimates.size: MBG and NC State 12-25 x 8-18 ft. 25 x 13 ft.
estimates.origin: A natural hybrid of I. cassine and I. opaca, first found wild in Florida in the 1920s. Recorded with its wild range, provenance 'hybrid', which keeps it out of both native modes.

estimates.size: MBG 20-30 x 10-20 ft. 25 x 12 ft, narrower than the hybrid at large; NC State: 'densely pyramidal'.
MBG 10-20 x 8-15 ft; UF 30-45 x 6-10 ft. 25 x 10 ft between them.
estimates.habit: MBG: narrow, columnar to open pyramidal; found in Savannah, Georgia, in commerce since 1953.

estimates.size: NC State 30-75 x 30-75 ft; 30-60 x 20-60 ft in a nursery library. 40 x 35 ft.
estimates.zones: NC State 7a-9b; nursery library 7a-10b, and its native range reaches coastal zone 10. 7-10.
estimates.bloom: NC State April-May; Wikipedia winter to early spring. March-April.
estimates.disease: NC State: the primary host of the sudden oak death pathogen.

estimates.size: MBG 35-50 x 20-35 ft, around 50 x 35 ft at maturity. 45 x 25 ft.
estimates.habit: MBG: straight central trunk, open-branched pyramid, rusty-brown leaf undersides.

estimates.size: 16-20 x 10-12 ft in most listings. 20 x 12 ft.
